corpus_accounting_detail.identity: official Wikipedia curid (record 'id'), exact string; node_id = 2wiki:c<curid>
corpus_accounting_detail.raw_source_record_unit: one json article record (one line of para_with_hyperlink.jsonl)
corpus_accounting_detail.text_construction: text = ' '.join(official 'sentences' list) -- identical to build.py::build_corpus_2wiki's rule (build.py:137), applied to the full article universe instead of the context union

phase_c_divergence.meaning: canonical_v1's text differs from the already-encoded 2wiki_universe text in exactly one situation and no other: scratchpad/build_2wiki_universe.py:42 applied .strip() to the same ' '.join(sentences) and canonical_v1 does not.  Every other record's encoder input is byte-identical -- hence token-identical -- to the stored row.  This count is therefore the exact upper bound on dense/SPLADE rows needing a re-encode: measured, not assumed.

empty_text_nodes.policy: KEPT -- dropping them would make corpus membership depend on a text-quality filter (the 2wiki_universe manifest observed 87,765)

REPLACES.superseded_corpus: pooled question-context union of train/dev/test 'context' fields

corpus_accounting_detail.note: This is the benchmark's own distributed article universe, not a question by-product: the record schema carries no question/answer/supporting_facts field, and the 398,354 context titles are 6.7% of it.

query_stats._gold_policy: gold_refs = official supporting_facts TITLES (deduplicated, order preserved); resolution is exact title -> curid node via a single scan of the frozen corpus. PER-REFERENCE semantics: each ref must map to >=1 canonical node. A title matching several curids is first disambiguated against the question's OWN official context paragraph and, when that identifies one uniquely, exactly that node is stored; only a genuinely ambiguous ref keeps its alternatives, and it is then satisfied DISJUNCTIVELY (retrieved & {alts} != {}), never conjunctively. Unresolvable titles are REPORTED, never rescued by adding the article to the corpus.

GOLD_SEMANTICS._semantics: gold ref -> {canonical node,...}; a ref resolves iff it maps to >=1 node; ALL_GOLD_REFS_RESOLVE = every ref in every gold-bearing split resolves; ambiguous refs are DISJUNCTIVE (retrieved & {alternatives} != {}), never conjunctive.
GOLD_SEMANTICS._supersedes: the cardinality test len(gold_node_ids)==len(set(gold_refs)), which failed a question merely because one of its refs legitimately expanded to >1 canonical node.
